verdict.tagline: A dark physics sandbox tempered by workshop security concerns.
for_you_if: you enjoy experimenting with physics-based sandbox contraptions
you like building and testing creative destruction scenarios
not_for_you_if: you rely heavily on Steam Workshop mods
you want to avoid potential malware and security risks

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring sandbox mechanics and physics for experimentation and building contraptions.

citations.review_text: This game is really good for tinkering with weird physics, mods (when the workshop comes back), or just blowing shit up. I just made a hyper sonic spike launcher that destroys anything it touches by shoving bombs into the back of a tube. I would highly recommend this game to anyone wanting to experiment with things, build, or just kill things.

I've played 52.2 hours of People Playground so far, and I'm still having a great time with it. The physics, sandbox mechanics and endless possibilities make it a really enjoyable game.

However, there's one feature I'd absolutely love to see: Multiplayer. Being able to experiment, build contraptions and mess around with friends would make this game even better.

Overall, a great game with tons of potential. Multiplayer would take it to the next level!
This is a very fun and acsessible game/sandbox where you can do anything!(Mods Included)
This game may look simple when you look at it but it's mechanics are really deep. You can create sophisticated creations. 8/10
Its a really fun sandbox game you can do ANYTHING i play it lots and make random scnerios :D

People Playground is an incredibly fun and entertaining sandbox game that offers endless possibilities for creativity and experimentation. The physics engine is impressive, and the wide variety of tools, objects, and mods makes every session feel unique. I love how much freedom the game gives you to experiment, build contraptions, and discover new ways to interact with the environment. The simple graphics work perfectly with the gameplay, and the game is surprisingly addictive. Overall, People Playground is a fantastic game with decent replayability and excellent value for money. Highly recommend it!

As far as it goes it is a very fun sandbox like simulator, but it is highly unstable, with it's workshop having had cases of viruses a total of three times already. That being said download mods at your own risk, the game itself is very nice.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that malware and hacking incidents have affected the Steam Workshop, leading to the removal or disabling of mods and contraptions.

citations.review_text: over 840 hours of peak modding gone to waste because of some bitch ass hackers, the games still peak tho

I really enjoyed this game but it keeps getting attacked by hackers. And now the workshop has been completely and utterly nuked which makes it really unfun (since alll my contraptions had mods)

Probably not an issue for someone new because they didnt get a taste of the mods. But losing them really made the game less fun

This used to be one of my favorite games, and it still is, but it has been subject to multiple virus attacks with little support from the developer, and even hostility. I don't think I can recommend this game without feeling like I'm being misleading. Still somewhat fun, but boring without the workshop and all the effort put into it over the years. I feel like I'm watching the beginning of the end. I'll probably keep playing it, but I don't think I can see myself being as passionate as before. It was nice while it lasted, goodbye people Playground. o7

Game is fun but considering it got back-to-back-to-BACK malware incidents in a startlingly small window (which caused the Workshop to be wiped) I seriously would not recommend buying it even during a sale. I would assume the dev(s) are doing what they can to make PPG safer going forward but until user safety is a lot more concrete, don't get it. Your data isn't worth the risk.

There was a time when People Playground was genuinely fun, thanks to its massive modding community.

However, the Steam Workshop suffered a malware incident, with malicious mods reportedly stealing valuable personal information from people who downloaded them.

What's even worse is that the entire Steam Workshop mod library was removed. Every single mod, including creations that people had spent hundreds of hours developing, was wiped. Years of community creativity and hard work GONE.

The game itself receives basically no updates, and honestly, without mods, People Playground becomes incredibly repetitive and boring. The modding community was what kept this game alive, constantly introducing new weapons, machines, contraptions and ways to play.

The developers have fully messed up this game forever as I don't believe this game is very special and could be remade but what made it special was the mods and that could not be replaced but now it has nothing.
